title: Cap. VI Arg. 5 close: fourth decree only intuits — so election from good pleasure, not foresight faith
pass_a_gloss: But the fourth decree, which alone deals with singular persons, does not bring certainty of salvation by way of an operating cause, but by way of foreseeing science: because God there does not determine efficaciously to produce faith and perseverance in the elect, but to intuit the same as already about to believe and persevere. Where therefore there is no certainty of salvation from God specially and infallibly causing, there is not that true election celebrated in the Scriptures. Therefore election hangs from the mere good pleasure of God, not from foresighted faith.
pass_b_english: The fourth decree alone touches singular persons — and even it gives certainty only as foreseeing knowledge, not as an operating cause: God does not there resolve to produce faith and perseverance in the elect, but only to regard them as already about to believe and persevere. Where salvation is not certain from God specially and infallibly causing, there is not the election Scripture celebrates. So election hangs on mere good pleasure, not foresighted faith.
source_text: Quartum vero decretum, quod solum de singularibus personis agit, certitudinem salutis non affert per modum causae operantis, sed per modum scientiae praevidentis: quia Deus ibi non statuit fidem et perseverantiam in electis efficaciter producere, sed eosdem tanquam jam credituros et perseveraturos intueri. Ubi igitur nulla est certitudo salutis ex Deo specialiter et infallibiliter causante, ibi non est vera illa electio Scripturis celebrata. Ergo electio pendet ex mero Dei beneplacito, non ex fide praevisa.
